'''''Marginatocereus marginatus''''' is a species of plant in the family [[Cactaceae]]. It is sometimes called '''Mexican fencepost cactus'''.<ref name=MFP/>

==Description==
It has tree-shaped columnar trunks that grow slowly to {{convert|12|ft|m}} and may reach {{convert|20|ft|m}} in height, rarely branching. Stems are {{convert|3|to|4|in|cm|abbr=off}} in diameter, with ribs {{convert|4|to|7|in|cm|abbr=on}}. Its central spine is about {{convert|3/8|in|cm}} in diameter with five to 9 radials and slightly yellowish in color. The five to nine marginal spines are 2 to 4 millimeters long. The large [[areole]]s on it later merge. The flowering areoles located near the shoot tips are covered with numerous bristles up to 2 centimeters long.{{Citation needed|date=July 2024}}

The funnel-shaped, reddish flowers are 3 to 4 centimeters long. Their pericarpel and floral tube are covered with scales that carry wool and bristles in their axils. The spherical fruits are more or less dry. They reach a diameter of up to 4 centimeters and are covered with slightly sloping thorns and wool.<ref name="Anderson Eggli 2005 p.  491">{{cite book | last=Anderson | first=Edward F. | last2=Eggli | first2=Urs | title=Das grosse Kakteen-Lexikon | publisher=Ulmer | publication-place=Stuttgart (Hohenheim) | date=2005 | isbn=3-8001-4573-1 | language=de | page= 491}}</ref>

Its cuttings are sometimes used to create fences, as its spines are not as large or dangerous as some cacti.<ref name=MFP>{{cite web|title=Mexican Fencepost Cactus.|url=http://www.delange.org/CactusMFencepost/CactusMFencepost.htm|website=Xeriscape Landscaping Plants For The Arizona Desert Environment. Pictures, Photos, Information, Descriptions|access-date=11 March 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180827075240/https://delange.org/CactusMFencepost/CactusMFencepost.htm|archive-date=27 August 2018|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Distribution==
The species is native to [[Mexico states]] of [[Hidalgo (state) |Hidalgo]], [[State of Mexico |México]], [[Guanajuato]], [[Querétaro]], [[Morelos]], [[Puebla]], [[Oaxaca]], [[Colima]], [[Michoacán]], and [[Guerrero]].<ref name=POWO/> It is also found in [[U.S. states]] that [[Borders of Mexico |border Mexico]]: [[Texas]], [[New Mexico]], [[Arizona]], and [[Southern California]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://apps.cals.arizona.edu/arboretum/taxon.aspx?id=20 | title = ''Pachycereus marginatus'' | publisher = University of Arizona }}</ref>

==Taxonomy==
The first description as ''Cereus marginatus'' was made in 1828 by [[Augustin Pyramus de Candolle|Augustin-Pyrame de Candolle]].<ref name="D&Amp (France) 1828 w912">{{cite web | last=D&Amp | first=Um National | last2=(France) | first2=histoire naturelle | title=Mémoires du Muséum d'histoire naturelle | publisher=G. Dufour | volume=t.17 (1828) | date=1828 | url=https://www.biodiversitylibrary.org/page/35009719 | access-date=2023-11-02}}</ref> The specific epithet marginatus comes from Latin, means 'bordered' and refers to the 'edges' formed by the [[areole |areoles]] that flow together on the ribs. [[Salvador Arias]] and [[Teresa Terrazas]] placed the species in the genus ''[[Lophocereus]]'' in 2009.<ref name="Arias Terrazas 2009 pp. 68–83">{{cite journal | last=Arias | first=Salvador | last2=Terrazas | first2=Teresa | title=Taxonomic Revision of ''Pachycereus'' (Cactaceae) | journal=Systematic Botany | publisher=American Society of Plant Taxonomists | volume=34 | issue=1 | date=2009-03-01 | issn=0363-6445 | doi=10.1600/036364409787602384 | pages=68–83}}</ref>
